Arabic has 28 letters. Of these 14 are called solar letters, and the other 14 are called

lunar letters.

In the articulation of the solar letters the tip or the blade of the tongue is involved

as in t. 1.1. s, etc. The tip or the blade of the tongue does not play any part in the

articulation of the lunar letters as b, w, m, k, etc.

When « J |» is prefixed to a noun beginning with a solar letter the « J »

of « J |» is assimilated to the solar letter, e.g. al-shamsu (the sun) is pronounced

ash-shamsu.

No change takes place in writing ( ‏لشمسُ‎ |). The assimilation is indicated by the

shaddah on the first letter of the noun.

No such assimilation takes place with the lunar letters, e.g., al-qamaru (the moon)

is pronounced al-gamaru (od) ).
